extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: The first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark for MLLMs in Video analysis, featuring 900 videos across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, spanning short to long durations (11 seconds to 1 hour), with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions manually annotated by expert annotators.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, Artistic Performance, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos with varying duration lengths were collected, including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes). Meta-information such as subtitles and audios were also obtained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions that could be answered solely based on textual questions without video content were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro. QA pairs that did not meet the criterion of requiring video content were returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, contributing to a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions encompass 12 distinct task types, including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair is designed to be closely tied to the video content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair underwent examination by a different annotator to verify that (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate. Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset reveals that MLLMs exhibit a general decline in performance with increasing video length, suggesting that limitations in processing longer video sequences could be a critical bottleneck. The long-tailed distribution of long video data poses challenges for acquisition.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for video understanding capabilities across diverse scenarios, temporal dynamics, and multimodal inputs. The benchmark is designed to assess perception, reasoning, and information synthesis capabilities.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Video-MME, the first-ever full-spectrum, MultiModal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis.

description.evidence: We introduce Video-MME, the first-ever full-spectrum, MultiModal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. Our work distinguishes from existing benchmarks through four key features: 1) Diversity in video types, spanning 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields to ensure broad scenario generalizability; 2) Duration in temporal dimension, encompassing both short-, medium-, and long-term videos, ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour, for robust contextual dynamics; 3) Breadth in data modalities, integrating multi-modal inputs besides video frames, including subtitles and audios, to unveil the all-round capabilities of MLLMs; 4) Quality in annotations, utilizing rigorous manual labeling by expert annotators to facilitate precise and reliable model assessment.

We identify 6 key domains: Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, and Multilingual, informed by popular trends on YouTube. Each domain is further subdivided into specific tags, such as football and basketball under Sports Competition, yielding a total of 30 finely-grained video categories... For each category, we collect videos with varying duration lengths, including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes). Besides, we also obtain corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios for in-depth investigation.
